newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EMU stability council must be informal - Santer.
newsitem.headline: EMU stability council must be informal - Santer.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer rejected on Saturday France's proposal to create a political counterweight to the European Central Bank overseeing the planned single currency.

"In my personal opinion the stability council cannot be allowed to affect the independent status of the European Central Bank," Santer told reporters at the World Economic Forum, adding that such a body could have "only an informal character".
Santer added that it was time to stop the debate over whether politicians should have a big say in monetary policy once the single currency is launched in 1999.

"I think it would be useful at this time if one would not enter into further debate about the position of the European Central Bank," he said. "The position of the European Central Bank is clearly defined in the Maastricht Treaty and one may not upset it."

In Davos for the annual gathering of business and political leaders, Santer said the single currency project was "irreversible" and strict financial criteria for countries seeking to qualify would not be watered down.
"We are sticking to the tight criteria of Maastricht," he said. "There will be no flexibility in this respect."
